places.name: Ted Peters Famous Smoked Fish
places.hours_text: Wed–Sun 11:30 AM–7:30 PM; closed Mon and Tue
places.summary: Smoked-fish restaurant at its current site since 1951: fish are laid on racks and smoked over red oak for 4 to 6 hours, and the German potato salad recipe from the early years is still served. The restaurant says the family business now spans five generations.
places.quote: Fresh fish are carefully laid on racks and smoked over a smoldering fire of red oak.

heritage.story: After World War II, Ted Peters set up a smoker on Blind Pass Road in front of his Blue Anchor restaurant so passing drivers could see and smell the fish. By 1951 Ted Peters Famous Smoked Fish was running at its current location, with his half-brother Elry Lathrop as a partner. Tilla Lathrop created the German potato salad recipe still served today, and later generations of both families have run the business.
heritage.visiting: Open to the public as a restaurant, Wednesday to Sunday.

places.notes: The building is in the city of South Pasadena (Census match: 1350 PASADENA AVE S, SOUTH PASADENA, FL 33707); the restaurant gives its mailing city as Saint Petersburg. Filed under west-stpete as the nearest St. Pete area.

places.name: The Chattaway
places.price_text: Afternoon tea (by reservation, 48 hours' notice, 12:30–3:30): adults $45, ages 16 and under $25
places.summary: Neighborhood restaurant in Old Town St. Petersburg with a garden patio, a small stage for local musicians and an indoor English tea room; afternoon tea is by reservation. The restaurant says it has been part of the community in one form or another for over 90 years.
places.quote: One of the biggest surprises of all is a trip indoors to feel like you’re stepping off the boat into a genuine English Tea Room.
places.notes: Visit St. Pete-Clearwater's landmark-restaurants list says it opened in 1951; the restaurant's own page says 'over 90 years' in one form or another. Summary uses the restaurant's wording. Opening hours are not on the home page.

places.name: Harvey's 4th Street Grill
places.hours_text: Sun 9 AM–9 PM; Mon–Wed 11:30 AM–9 PM; Thu–Fri 11:30 AM–10 PM; Sat 9 AM–10 PM
places.summary: Bar and grill open since April 1, 1984, serving fresh Gulf grouper, steaks and Sunday brunch. The restaurant says much of its decor came from historic St. Pete hotels, including the Vinoy, the Soreno and the Albemarle.
places.quote: Harvey’s 4th Street Grill is a West Coast Florida style bar and grill. We feature fresh grouper and steak, Sunday brunch, and full moon celebrations.
places.notes: Phone from the Visit St. Pete-Clearwater profile. The site spells the hotel 'Albermarle'.

places.name: Teak
places.address: 800 2nd Ave NE (Pier Point, 4th floor, St. Pete Pier)
places.summary: Restaurant on the fourth floor of the Pier Point building at the end of the St. Pete Pier, serving lunch, dinner and weekend brunch built on coastal flavors and Gulf seafood. Pier Teaki (rooftop bar) and Driftwood Cafe (grab-and-go) are in the same building.
places.quote: serves lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch with a menu inspired by coastal flavors and Gulf seafood
places.notes: Reservations through OpenTable per teakstpete.com. Hours are not published on the pages read. Coordinates are the Pier Point building at the end of the pier. Coordinates: the OpenStreetMap point for Pier Teaki at the end of the pier (Teak is one floor below).

places.name: Pier Teaki
places.address: 800 2nd Ave NE, 5th floor (Pier Point, St. Pete Pier)
places.hours_text: Mon–Fri 11 AM–11:59 PM; Sat–Sun 10 AM–midnight (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Tiki-style rooftop bar on top of the Pier Point building at the end of the St. Pete Pier, serving tropical cocktails and shareable bites, with private huts looking at the skyline and Tampa Bay. It is run by the owners of The Birchwood and turns 21-and-up after hours, per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater.
places.notes: Coordinates: the OpenStreetMap point for Pier Teaki at the end of the pier (Teak is one floor below).

places.name: Doc Ford's Rum Bar & Grille, St. Pete Pier
places.hours_text: Daily 11 AM–10 PM
places.summary: Restaurant and rum bar at the base of the St. Pete Pier serving Florida fare and Caribbean flavors, with indoor seats and seawall seating facing downtown and Tampa Bay. The name comes from a character in Randy Wayne White's novels; the other two Doc Ford's are on Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach.
places.quote: Our name comes from a character in a series of books by Randy Wayne White, but has since grown to an award winning restaurant with national accolades.

places.name: The Canopy at The Birchwood
places.hours_text: Tue–Thu 4 PM–midnight; Fri 3 PM–2 AM; Sat 11 AM–2 AM; Sun 11 AM–midnight; closed Mon (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Rooftop bar and lounge on The Birchwood hotel on Beach Drive, with craft cocktails, bar bites and views over Tampa Bay. The hotel says the building went up in 1924 as the Lantern Lane Apartments; its restaurant Birch & Vine is downstairs.
places.notes: The Birchwood itself is a hotel (stays slices).

places.name: Columbia Restaurant, Sand Key
places.hours_text: Sun–Thu 11 AM–9 PM; Fri–Sat 11 AM–10 PM
places.summary: Sand Key branch of the Columbia, the Spanish-Cuban restaurant family founded in Ybor City in 1905, with a Mediterranean-style dining room and an outdoor deck on the Intracoastal Waterway. The company calls itself Florida's oldest restaurant.
places.quote: Choose a table looking out onto the Intracoastal Waterway from the Mediterranean dining room, or experience the casual atmosphere from our outdoor deck on the water.

places.name: Columbia Restaurant, St. Armands Circle
places.hours_text: Sun–Thu 11 AM–9 PM; Fri–Sat 11 AM–10 PM
places.summary: St. Armands Circle branch of the Columbia, the Spanish-Cuban restaurant family founded in Ybor City in 1905, a short walk from Lido Beach. The Columbia calls this location the oldest operating restaurant in Sarasota.
places.quote: Relax in one of our Mediterranean-style dining rooms or enjoy an outdoor table on the patio while sampling our award-winning Spanish/Cuban cuisine at the oldest operating restaurant in Sarasota.

places.name: Crabby's Beachside Pavilion
places.hours_text: Sun–Thu 8 AM–10 PM; Fri–Sat 8 AM–11 PM; breakfast daily 8–11 AM
places.summary: Open-air beachfront restaurant and bar on Clearwater Beach, serving seafood, burgers and cocktails with live music on the deck. Beachside Hospitality Group took it over after nearly 65 years of Hamilton family stewardship and calls it the oldest beach pavilion in Florida.
places.quote: As the oldest beach pavilion in Florida approaches its 100-year milestone, one thing remains clear: the Pavilion has always been about more than just a building.
places.notes: Visit St. Pete-Clearwater dates it to 1926 (first a snack concession with lockers and bath houses) and says it operated as the Palm Pavilion. Phone from that profile.

places.name: Bob Heilman's Beachcomber
places.summary: Family-owned restaurant on Clearwater Beach since 1948, serving seafood, steaks, wine and classic cocktails with live piano music daily; Bobby's Bistro is part of the same business.
places.quote: Taste the tradition in an elegant setting, accompanied by live piano music daily.

places.name: Frenchy's Rockaway Grill
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 11 AM–10 PM; Fri–Sat 11 AM–11 PM; Sun 11 AM–10 PM (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Open-air restaurant on the sand at Clearwater Beach serving Gulf seafood, including Frenchy's grouper sandwich, with two bars and live music daily. It is one of several Frenchy's restaurants on the beach; the first, Frenchy's Original Cafe, opened in 1981, per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater.
places.notes: frenchysonline.com blocked both WebFetch and curl (bot challenge), so the tourism profile is the source. Its hours are current on that profile; no closure notice there. I Love the Burg (Nov 10, 2024) reported the Rockaway Grill was still recovering from Hurricanes Helene and Milton while the Saltwater Cafe and the original cafe had reopened; the tourism profile now lists regular hours. Michael 'Frenchy' Preston opened the first Frenchy's in 1981, per that article.

places.name: The Original Crabby Bill's
places.hours_text: Main restaurant daily 11 AM–10 PM; outdoor Loading Dock daily 11 AM–11 PM
places.summary: Family seafood restaurant the Loder family opened in Indian Rocks Beach on April 28, 1983, with a main dining room and an outdoor bar, the Loading Dock, with live music. There are also Crabby Bill's locations in St. Pete Beach and Palm Harbor.
places.quote: Daughter Eleanor had the winning idea: “Dad is crabby, we like crabs, why not Crabby Bill’s?”
places.notes: The contact page prints the ZIP as 33706; the ZIP here comes from the Census match. Live-music calendar on the home page runs through late Sep 2026, so it is operating.

places.name: The Hurricane Seafood Restaurant
places.hours_text: Lunch and dinner Sun–Thu 11:30 AM–9:30 PM, Fri–Sat 11:30 AM–10 PM; breakfast Fri–Sun 8–11 AM
places.summary: Seafood restaurant on Gulf Way in Pass-a-Grille, opened in 1977 by the Falkenstein family on the site of the old Casa Bonita Hotel; its Hurricane Watch rooftop deck has twin bars and 360-degree views.
places.quote: In 1977, the Hurricane Seafood Restaurant opened its doors at the site of the old Casa Bonita Hotel in Pass-A-Grille Beach.
places.notes: The site says the hotel site earlier held Page's Pavilion, a bathhouse built in 1912; the family expanded the first floor in 1986 and added the upper floors and rooftop bar in 1990.

places.name: IL Ritorno
places.hours_text: Sun 5–9 PM; Mon–Thu 5–9:30 PM; Fri–Sat 5–10:30 PM; closed Christmas, New Year's Day, July 4, Thanksgiving and Super Bowl Sunday
places.summary: Modern Italian dinner restaurant on Central Avenue run by owner and executive chef David Benstock; the name means "The Return" and marks his homecoming to St. Pete. It is a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida. Dress code is business casual.
places.quote: IL Ritorno creates modern Italian dishes for the discerning palate, introducing new and interesting flavor combinations that add elegance to a traditionally rustic cuisine.
places.notes: MICHELIN Guide Florida 2026 (announced May 28, 2026) lists 'Il Ritorno, 449 Central Ave. N., #101, St. Petersburg, 33701' among recommended restaurants (the list is an image on the Michelin press page).

places.name: Sushi Sho Rexley
places.hours_text: Thu–Sun 5–9 PM; closed Mon–Wed
places.summary: Small omakase sushi counter downtown where dinner is a set chef's menu, booked and prepaid through the restaurant's site; seats are limited and the omakase starts on time. It is a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: Omakase takes times to prepare and seats are very limited.
places.notes: Visit St. Pete-Clearwater says the counter seats 10 and chef Rexley Kwok trained under Hiro Ida. The site's structured data lists slightly different hours (Wed–Sun) from its visible text (Thu–Sun 5–9); the visible text is used.

places.name: Fortu
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 5–9 PM; Fri–Sat 5–10 PM; Sun 5–9 PM
places.summary: Japanese-inspired restaurant downtown serving modern Asian small plates meant for sharing, with a cocktail program. It is a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida; Visit St. Pete-Clearwater places it in the historic Ponce de Leon Hotel.
places.quote: Our menu celebrates Japan's culinary spirit through the lens of worldwide influence, designed as small plates meant to be shared and composed from meticulously sourced ingredients.

places.name: in between days
places.summary: Sake and vinyl listening bar in a small house on 1st Avenue South, modeled on Tokyo's listening bars, serving sake, French-style oysters and small plates. It was added as a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: Inspired by the underground listening bars of Tokyo, our little house is warmed by pair of 1972 Klipsch Cornwalls that adorn the back of the bar paired with two turn-tables and a diverse vinyl collection.
places.notes: Hours differ between the site's structured data (Wed–Sat 5–10 PM) and Visit St. Pete-Clearwater (Wed–Sat 5–11 PM, Sun 5–10 PM), so hours are left unknown. Phone from the tourism profile.

places.name: Elliott Aster
places.hours_text: Tue–Sun: main dining 4:30–10 PM, lounge and bar 4–11 PM; Sunday brunch 10:30 AM–2 PM
places.summary: Restaurant in The Vinoy hotel run with chef Lee Wolen and Boka Restaurant Group; Visit St. Pete-Clearwater describes wood-fired steaks, seafood, house-made pasta and an antipasti bar. It was added as a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: A collaboration between The Vinoy, Chef Lee Wolen, and Boka Restaurant Group, brings refined dining to St. Petersburg.
places.notes: The Vinoy itself is a historic hotel (stays slices).

places.name: The Tides Market
places.hours_text: Mon–Fri 11 AM–9 PM; Sat–Sun 10 AM–9 PM
places.summary: Family-owned seafood market and eatery on Main Street run by Jon and Mary Kate Walker, selling fresh seafood, meats, produce and groceries and serving meals, brunch and boutique oysters. No reservations (groups of 8 or more can call ahead). It is a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: Nestled in the heart of Safety Harbor, The Tides Market is your neighborhood spot for fresh seafood, all-natural meats, locally grown produce, and thoughtfully curated goods and groceries.

places.name: Lucky 8
places.summary: Southern comfort-food restaurant in Sarasota's Southside Village from chef Mark Majorie, inspired by New Orleans neighborhood eateries. It was named a Bib Gourmand (good food at a good value) in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida, one of three Sarasota restaurants that WWSB reported as the city's first Michelin recognition.
places.notes: lucky8srq.com (the site Visit Sarasota links) returned a bot challenge to both WebFetch and curl, so hours and phone are unknown. Address from the Michelin 2026 Bib Gourmand table. 'First Michelin recognition for Sarasota' per WWSB (mysuncoast.com), which names Lucky 8, Tralia and Focaccia. Visit Sarasota's article describes chef Mark Majorie's New Orleans-inspired Southern comfort food; two WebFetch reads returned different wording, so no quote is used.

places.name: Focaccia Sandwich + Bakery
places.hours_text: Tue–Sat 8 AM–4 PM
places.summary: Bakery and sandwich shop from chef Nick Sammelman that bakes its own focaccia loaves and builds breakfast and lunch sandwiches on them. It was added as a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: Bringing joy to people through artisan crafted sandwiches, on house made focaccia with clean, wholesome ingredients.

places.name: Tralia
places.summary: Pizzeria in Sarasota's Gulf Gate area from chef Anthony Petralia, who began with a one-day-a-week pop-up; it serves Detroit-style and round pies. It was added as a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: Our goal is simple. Bring the best quality ingredients and preparation to the forefront of our service at Tralia.
places.notes: The site shows two different sets of hours (Mon–Thu 11–10, Fri–Sat 11–11, Sun 11–10 vs. Fri–Sat 11–12, Sun 10–10), so hours are left unknown.

places.name: Nineteen61
places.hours_text: Lunch Mon–Sat 11 AM–3 PM; dinner Mon–Wed 5–9 PM, Thu–Sat 5–10 PM; Sunday brunch 10 AM–2:30 PM and dinner 4–8 PM
places.summary: Downtown Lakeland restaurant with a rooftop bar from owner and chef Marcos Fernandez, cooking modern Spanish food with Latin American and Southern touches. It was added as a recommended restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Florida.
places.quote: The menu is full of memorable items that combine a modern Spanish style accompanied by a Latin American twist with a Southern propensity.

places.name: Hellas Restaurant & Bakery
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 11 AM–9 PM; Fri–Sat 11 AM–10 PM; Sun 11 AM–9 PM (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Greek restaurant and pastry bakery on the Sponge Docks, run by the Karterouliotis family since 1970; the menu runs from gyros and Greek salads to lamb chops and local seafood, and the bakery sells Greek pastries to eat in or take away.
places.quote: At Hellas Restaurant & Bakery, our family has been serving authentic Greek food and pastries for over 50 years.

places.name: Mykonos Restaurant
places.hours_text: Daily 11 AM–10 PM (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Greek restaurant on the Sponge Docks known for grilled seafood and meats, including grilled octopus, with indoor and outdoor seating. Visit St. Pete-Clearwater lists it among the area's landmark restaurants, established in 1992.
places.notes: No official website found; the tourism profile links a Facebook page. The landmark list credits founder Andreas Salivaras. Status taken from the tourism profile's current hours; not independently confirmed.

places.name: Dimitri's on the Water
places.summary: Greek seafood and steak restaurant on the Sponge Docks with indoor and covered outdoor seating looking at the local fishing and sponge boats.
places.notes: dimitrisonthewater.com returned a bot challenge; facts from the tourism profile, which lists hours for every day but Wednesday, so hours are left unknown.

places.name: Rusty Bellies Waterfront Grill
places.summary: Family-owned seafood restaurant with an outdoor tiki bar and live music directly on the Anclote River by the Sponge Docks; the family's boats supply it, and its seafood market, Pelican Point Seafood, is next door.
places.quote: Family-owned and operated restaurant, outdoor bar, working waterfront, and fresh seafood market. Located directly on the Anclote River.

places.name: Tarpon Springs Distillery
places.summary: Small-batch distillery founded by Lisa and Barry Butler that makes whiskey, moonshine, gin, aquavit and Papou's Ouzo; it offers tours and tastings and has a bar and an outdoor music venue, The Rye Bar. Visit St. Pete-Clearwater says it is in a renovated historic sponge warehouse.
places.quote: Our spirits are crafted with heart, heritage, and a bit of Florida’s coastal magic.
places.notes: Hours differ between the site's structured data (Wed–Thu 1–6, Fri–Sat 1–10, Sun 1–6) and the tourism profile (open daily, longer hours), so hours are left unknown. The tourism profile says tours and tastings run every half hour 1–5 PM at no charge; not confirmed on the distillery's own pages read.

places.name: Dunedin Brewery
places.hours_text: Mon–Tue 11 AM–9 PM; Wed 11 AM–11 PM; Thu 11 AM–10 PM; Fri–Sat 11 AM–midnight; Sun 11 AM–8 PM
places.summary: Brewpub in downtown Dunedin brewing since 1996, with pub food and live music on two stages (the Pub Stage and the Moon Tower). The brewery calls itself Florida's oldest craft brewery, which it defines as the oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation.
places.quote: We weren't the first to make beer in Florida, but we're the oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation.
places.notes: The 'oldest' claim is the brewery's own and is qualified on its page (first line of the quote); the header also says 'FL's Oldest Microbrewery'.

places.name: 7venth Sun Brewery
places.hours_text: Sun–Thu noon–10 PM; Fri–Sat noon–midnight
places.summary: Woman-owned brewery a half block off the Pinellas Trail in downtown Dunedin, known for sours and hoppy beers; a 3.5-barrel system feeds ten taps, and the flagship is Graffiti Orange, a creamsicle wheat. It held its soft opening on December 2, 2011.
places.quote: 7venth Sun is woman owned and brewed just a half block off the Pinellas Trail in charming downtown Dunedin.

places.name: Caledonia Brewing
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 2 PM–midnight; Fri–Sat noon–midnight; Sun noon–10 PM; 21 and up after 8 PM
places.summary: Small-batch brewery opened April 6, 2017, in the 1924 Dunedin Times building on Main Street; its name and unicorn logo nod to Dunedin's Scottish heritage, and it is known for Rat Arsed Scotch Ale. The taproom has community tables and a covered, pet-friendly patio.
places.quote: Caledonia is name given to Scotland by the Romans and is a nod to the local Scottish heritage here in Dunedin (Sterling Scotland is our sister city).

places.name: The Restorative
places.hours_text: Wed–Sat 5–8 PM (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Small dinner restaurant opened in 2017 by husband-and-wife chef-owners Jason and Erin "Cricket" Borajkiewicz, with a chef's counter facing the open kitchen and a short, frequently changing menu built on Florida ingredients. The restaurant cites Tampa Bay Times Top 30 listings for 2024 and 2025.
places.quote: Husband and wife Chef Owners Jason & Erin "Cricket" Borajkiewicz create a small, ever changing menu focusing on ingredients made in Florida.

places.name: Bon Appétit Restaurant
places.hours_text: Sun–Thu 11 AM–9 PM; Fri–Sat 11 AM–10 PM
places.summary: Waterfront restaurant and marina bar at the Dunedin marina, open since 1976, with weekend brunch and live entertainment. It is part of the Original Crabby Bill's family of restaurants.
places.quote: Bon Appétit Restaurant has been Dunedin’s choice for waterfront dining since its opening in 1976.
places.parking_text: Free on-site parking; valet Friday and Saturday
places.notes: Opening year, hours, address and parking come from the site-wide footer text shown on bonappetitrestaurant.com pages.

places.name: Hi-Fi Rooftop Bar
aliases: Hi-Fi Rooftop Bar at the Fenway Hotel
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 4–10 PM; Fri 4–11 PM; Sat 2–11 PM; Sun 2–10 PM
places.summary: Cocktail bar on the roof of the Fenway Hotel on Edgewater Drive in Dunedin; seating is first come, first served, with no reservations. The hotel says the original Fenway speakeasy was in the basement.
places.quote: The original Fenway speakeasy was located in the basement. This rooftop Dunedin bar brings cocktails to new heights.
places.notes: The Fenway Hotel itself is a stay (stays slices).

places.name: 3 Daughters Brewing
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 11:30 AM–10 PM; Fri–Sat 11:30 AM–midnight; Sun 11:30 AM–8 PM
places.summary: Brewery and warehouse tasting room that opened in December 2013, with 42 rotating taps of its own beer, cider, seltzer and sangria and a stage for live entertainment. A second tasting room with its own brewing system opened in March 2022 on the third floor of 381 Mandalay Ave., Clearwater Beach, looking over Pier 60.
places.quote: How many beers does it take to put three daughters through college?
places.notes: The company says it has grown into one of the largest independent breweries in Florida; not repeated in the summary. The Clearwater Beach tasting room page gives daily hours 11 AM–10 PM.

places.name: Green Bench Brewing Company
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu noon–10 PM; Fri–Sat noon–midnight; Sun noon–9 PM
places.summary: Brewery with a tasting room and beer garden on Baum Avenue North; its owners say they opened St. Petersburg's first microbrewery, after starting construction in 2013. The company also runs Webb's City Cellar, a mead and cider bar.
places.quote: Our doors, our bars, our benches, are open to everyone.

places.name: St. Pete Brewing Co.
places.hours_text: Sun noon–10 PM; Mon–Tue 2–10 PM; Wed–Thu 2 PM–midnight; Fri–Sat noon–late
places.summary: Downtown brewery and taproom on 1st Avenue North, pouring its own beers such as Grateful Stout and a Scottish ale.
places.quote: Born of a desire to provide beer enthusiasts a beer choice that exemplifies the essence of St. Petersburg, FL.

places.name: St. Petersburg Distillery
places.hours_text: Tasting room Wed and Sun 10:30 AM–6 PM, Thu–Sat 10:30 AM–11 PM; speakeasy Thu–Sat 6–11 PM
places.summary: Family-owned craft distillery making spirits in small batches since 2014, just off the Pinellas Trail, with a tasting room, a 1920s-themed speakeasy and guided tours (21 and up for tastings), including an evening Moonshiners Tour about Prohibition-era rum running.
places.quote: St. Petersburg Distillery—a proudly local, family-owned distillery that has been perfecting the art of craft spirits since 2014.
places.notes: Tour hours per the tour page: distillery tour Thu–Sun 11 AM–4 PM on the hour; Moonshiners Tour Thu–Sat 6–9 PM on the hour (60 minutes). Tours are also in the exp-land slice.

places.name: Pinellas Ale Works
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu 3–10 PM; Fri–Sat noon–midnight; Sun noon–8 PM
places.summary: Brewery, tap room and beer garden that welcomes dogs and hosts regular events benefiting Pinellas County animal charities; a second taproom, PAW Taps & Tails, is at 5518 Haines Rd.
places.quote: As its initials would suggest, PAW is one of the most dog-friendly breweries in St. Pete

places.name: Cage Brewing
places.summary: Grand Central District brewery with 20 taps, live bands most nights of the week and Kraken Joe's oak-fired brick-oven pizza made on site.
places.quote: Full bands, premier sound system, most nights of the week.

places.name: Gulfport Brewery + Eatery
places.summary: Brewery and kitchen in a beach bungalow in Gulfport's historic waterfront district, serving its own beers since 2020, including the Hippie Oasis IPA; Visit St. Pete-Clearwater notes it welcomes dogs.
places.quote: Located in The Gulfport historic waterFront District, Our BEACH Bungalow HAS BEEN SERVING UP AWARD WINNING BREWS, Food & Entertainment since 2020.

places.name: Mad Beach Craft Brewing Company
places.hours_text: Daily 11 AM–10 PM
places.summary: Brewpub restaurant on Village Boulevard in Madeira Beach pairing session beers and stronger brews with a Caribbean- and Southern-inspired menu; its event space has a balcony of over 1,000 square feet.
places.quote: a full brewpub restaurant specializing in beach friendly session-able beers by day, and go big or go home higher gravity beers
places.notes: The page says 'Located in the Heart of the Gulf Beaches'; the John's Pass Village location follows from its Village Blvd address. John's Pass businesses were hit by the 2024 hurricanes; the site shows current hours and events.

places.name: Anecdote Brewing Co.
places.hours_text: Summer hours: Mon–Thu 1–10 PM; Fri–Sun noon–10 PM
places.summary: Small-batch brewery on Gulf Boulevard in Indian Rocks Beach, a short walk from the beach, serving gluten-removed craft beers. It calls itself the closest brewery to the Gulf beach.
places.quote: The closest Brewery to the Gulf beach is in the heart of Indian Rocks Beach FL, just a stone’s throw away from the soft sands of the Gulf of Mexico

places.name: Grindhaus Brew Lab
places.hours_text: Thu 2–10 PM; Fri–Sat 2–11 PM; Sun 2–7 PM
places.summary: Boutique brewery and tap room in an industrial complex on Hercules Avenue in Clearwater, pouring cream ales and hard seltzers and hosting movie nights, pop-up markets and events.

places.name: Crooked Thumb Brewery
places.summary: Safety Harbor craft brewery with a tasting room and outdoor beer garden a block from Main Street, pouring lagers, IPAs and fruited sours from over 20 taps, with live music and food trucks. Its name comes from a local history's description of Pinellas County hanging off Florida's west coast like a crooked thumb, per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater.
places.quote: Lagers, IPAs, fruited sours and experimental brews rotate among over 20 taps.
places.notes: ZIP 34695 from the brewery's site (the tourism profile prints 34698).

places.name: Rapp Brewing Company
places.hours_text: Tue–Thu 3–10 PM; Fri 3 PM–midnight; Sat 2 PM–midnight; Sun 1–8 PM; closed Mon
places.summary: Brewery and tasting room opened in 2012 by brewmaster Gregory Rapp, with 40 changing taps, flights of 5-ounce pours and food trucks on rotation; the brewery keeps a yeast bank of over 25 strains.
places.quote: Our 40 taps are always changing!

places.name: Brighter Days Brewing Company
places.hours_text: Mon–Thu noon–9 PM; Fri noon–10 PM; Sat 11 AM–10 PM; Sun 11 AM–7 PM (per Visit St. Pete-Clearwater)
places.summary: Brewery next to the Pinellas Trail in downtown Tarpon Springs with a walk-up window, an open-air garage-door room and a patio, geared to cyclists and walkers; it serves sessionable beers and hosts live music.
places.notes: brighterdaysbrewing.com did not respond; the tourism profile links only an Instagram account.

places.name: Guppy's on the Beach
places.hours_text: Daily 11:30 AM–9:30 PM; early dinner menu daily 4–5:15 PM
places.summary: Seafood restaurant on Gulf Boulevard in Indian Rocks Beach serving local fish such as Gulf grouper piccata, Florida lobster tail and steaks; it has a dress code. It is one of three restaurants run by Eugen Fuhrmann's 3 Best Chefs, which says it has operated since 1985.
places.quote: We’re known for serving the freshest local seafood such as Local Gulf Grouper Picatta and Florida Lobster Tail, as well as classic cuts of beef such as New York Strip Steak and Boneless Beef Shortribs.

places.name: Salt Rock Grill
places.hours_text: Mon–Fri 4–10 PM; Sat–Sun noon–10 PM
places.summary: Steak and seafood restaurant in Indian Shores overlooking the Intracoastal Waterway, with prime and choice beef, day-boat seafood, a raw bar and a large wine cellar. It is part of Baystar Restaurant Group, which also runs Island Way Grill.
places.quote: Known for our hand cut U.S.D.A prime and choice grade beef, fresh dayboat caught seafood, raw bar and amazing wine cellar.

places.name: The Friendly Fisherman Seafood Restaurant
places.hours_text: Daily from 11 AM; closes 9 PM Sun–Thu, 10 PM Fri–Sat
places.summary: Seafood restaurant on the John's Pass boardwalk since 1978, serving Gulf grouper, shrimp and oysters, with a Dockside Lounge; anglers can bring in their catch and have the kitchen cook it.
places.quote: A John’s Pass staple since 1978, The Friendly Fisherman serves fresh Gulf seafood and Florida favorites prepared daily.
places.notes: Visit St. Pete-Clearwater says it opened in 1978 as the first restaurant at John's Pass. John's Pass was damaged in the 2024 hurricanes; the site shows current hours (page modified Feb 2026).

places.name: Paradise Grille (Pass-a-Grille)
places.hours_text: Daily 7 AM to half an hour after sunset
places.summary: Casual cafe on the sand at Pass-a-Grille Beach serving breakfast, lunch, dinner, beer and wine, with singer-songwriters playing Friday to Sunday and a crowd for the sunset. A second Paradise Grille is at 6850 Beach Plaza, St. Pete Beach.
places.quote: Paradise Grille is THE place to catch a famous Florida sunset, meet with friends or enjoy a fantastic meal.

places.name: Billy's Stone Crab Restaurant
places.summary: Waterfront seafood and steak restaurant in Tierra Verde on Hurricane Hole, open since 1972 in a building made of native cypress and pine; Visit St. Pete-Clearwater says stone crab from thousands of traps is served from October through May.

places.name: Star Fish Company
aliases: Star Fish Company Seafood Market & Dockside Restaurant
places.summary: Seafood market and dockside restaurant in the fishing village of Cortez, looking over Sarasota Bay toward Longboat Key. heritage.story: Star Fish Company was started in the early 1920s by Judge Millis. Gaylord Garner bought it in the 1950s, and a retail market selling locally caught seafood was added in the 1960s. Allen Garner sold the company in 1996 to Karen Bell, who began serving cooked seafood at picnic tables on the back dock.
heritage.visiting: Open to the public as a seafood market and casual dockside restaurant.

places.notes: Coordinates are the ones the business publishes in its structured data. places.name: Mar Vista Dockside Restaurant & Pub
places.hours_text: Daily 11 AM–9 PM
places.summary: Bayside seafood restaurant and pub under old buttonwood trees in the Longbeach village at the north end of Longboat Key, in one of the rusticated concrete-block houses Rufus Jordan built from about 1912; it has public boat slips and a covered deck.
places.quote: Discover the secret of island foodies and century-old buttonwood trees.

heritage.story: Beginning in about 1912, Longboat Key developer Rufus Jordan built early houses on the north end of the key from rusticated stone blocks, and the Mar Vista building is one of them; it survived the 1921 hurricane. After 1947 the property became a fish camp with a pub, and in the 1950s it grew into a popular restaurant and bar. Chiles Hospitality bought it in the 1980s to keep its Old Florida feel, and Beachside Hospitality Group bought it in 2024.

places.notes: Street address printed as '760 Broadway Street North' on the site.

places.quote: The tradition of entertainment and relaxation at the site dates back as far as 1911.

heritage.story: In the early 1900s visitors from Tampa came by boat to a pavilion on this beach. After a fire destroyed the pavilion in 1946, two old army barracks were placed on the spot and the Sandbar began; the 1950 hurricane badly damaged the building, which was rebuilt. Ed Chiles and partners bought the Sandbar in July 1979.

places.name: Rod & Reel Pier

places.status_note: The pier and its restaurant were washed away by Hurricane Milton (Oct 2024); only pilings and a memorial remain at the site. report:
# eat-pinellas: where to eat and drink in St. Pete, the Gulf beaches, Clearwater & North Pinellas, and day-trip towns

Checked 2026-09-27. 84 places (collection `places` only).

## What is covered

- **Historic and landmark restaurants**: Ted Peters Famous Smoked Fish (1951), The Chattaway, Harvey's 4th Street Grill (1984), El Cap, Skyway Jack's (1976), Bob Heilman's Beachcomber (1948), Crabby's Beachside Pavilion (the former Palm Pavilion), the Original Crabby Bill's (1983), The Hurricane (Pass-a-Grille, 1977), the Seahorse (Pass-a-Grille, 1938 building, rebuilt after Helene), Friendly Fisherman (John's Pass, 1978), Billy's Stone Crab (1972), O'Keefe's Tavern (1961), Bon Appétit (Dunedin, 1976), Casa Tina, Columbia Restaurant at Sand Key and at St. Armands Circle.
- **Frenchy's** (Clearwater Beach): Rockaway Grill and Saltwater Cafe. The Original Cafe and South Beach Cafe were left out (see below).
- **Tarpon Springs Sponge Docks Greek food**: Hellas Restaurant & Bakery (since 1970), Mykonos, Dimitri's on the Water, Mama's Greek Cuisine (1978), plus Rusty Bellies (seafood) and Tarpon Springs Distillery (ouzo, whiskey).
- **MICHELIN Guide Florida 2026** (announced May 28, 2026; first statewide guide). There are no starred restaurants in Pinellas, Sarasota or Polk. Recommended: Elliott Aster, Fortu, IL Ritorno, in between days and Sushi Sho Rexley (St. Pete); The Tides Market (Safety Harbor); Focaccia Sandwich + Bakery and Tralia (Sarasota); Nineteen61 (Lakeland). Bib Gourmand: Lucky 8 (Sarasota). Tags: michelin-recommended, michelin-bib-gourmand, michelin-2026. No Clearwater restaurant is in the 2026 selection.
- **Breweries and distilleries (18)**: Dunedin Brewery (its own claim, quoted and qualified: "the oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation" in Florida, brewing since 1996), 7venth Sun, Caledonia (Dunedin); 3 Daughters (St. Pete and Clearwater Beach), Green Bench (it says it was St. Pete's first microbrewery), St. Pete Brewing, Pinellas Ale Works, Cage, Gulfport Brewery, Mad Beach Brewing, Anecdote (Indian Rocks Beach), Grindhaus Brew Lab (Clearwater), Crooked Thumb (Safety Harbor), Rapp (Seminole), Brighter Days (Tarpon Springs); St. Petersburg Distillery and Tarpon Springs Distillery.
- **St. Pete Pier**: Teak, Pier Teaki (rooftop tiki bar), Doc Ford's, Fresco's.
- **Rooftop and cocktail bars**: The Canopy at The Birchwood, Pier Teaki, Hi-Fi Rooftop Bar (Fenway Hotel, Dunedin), Jimmy's Crow's Nest (Clearwater Beach), The Mandarin Hide, Gigglewaters (Safety Harbor, 1920s-themed bar with a classic-movie screen), COCKtail St. Pete (LGBTQ, Mari Jean Hotel).
- **Beach bars and waterfront**: Ka'Tiki (1982), Undertow, Mahuffer's, Shephard's Tiki Bar, Paradise Grille, Buoy's, O'Maddy's (Gulfport), Guppy's, Salt Rock Grill, Island Way Grill, Caretta on the Gulf, Maritana (Don CeSar).
- **Food hall**: Central Park St. Pete Food Hall (551 Central Ave, old Woolworth building; phased opening from Feb 2026).
- **Other St. Pete**: Bodega (Cuban sandwich), Parkshore Grill (Beach Drive since 1996), BellaBrava (2005).
- **Day trips**: Star Fish Company (Cortez, dates to the 1920s), Mar Vista (Longboat Key, c. 1912 building), Sandbar (Anna Maria, site history to 1911, bought 1979), Rod & Reel Pier (status below), Yoder's (Sarasota Amish cooking since 1975), Columbia St. Armands, and the four Michelin picks in Sarasota and Lakeland.

## Counts

- By kind: restaurant 54, brewery 16, bar 10, distillery-winery 2, cafe-bakery 1, food-hall 1.
- By region: St. Petersburg 29, Gulf Beaches 25, Clearwater & North Pinellas 20, Day Trips 10.
- By area: downtown-stpete 16, clearwater-beach 9, tarpon-springs 7, dunedin 7, grand-central 6, sarasota 5, indian-rocks-beach 5, bradenton-anna-maria 4, pass-a-grille 3, safety-harbor 3, st-pete-beach 3, south-stpete 2, old-northeast 2, gulfport 2, madeira-beach 2, downtown-clearwater 2, west-stpete 1, sand-key 1, polk 1, largo 1, fort-de-soto 1, treasure-island 1.
- Status: open 83, temporarily-closed 1 (Rod & Reel Pier). signature: true on 5 (Ted Peters, Frenchy's Rockaway Grill, The Hurricane, Hellas, Dunedin Brewery). Heritage blocks on 4 (Ted Peters, Star Fish Company, Mar Vista, Sandbar).
- Source: 73 records use the business's own page as source_url. 11 fall back to a Visit St. Pete-Clearwater profile or list because the business site blocked both fetchers or has no site (Frenchy's Rockaway, Billy's Stone Crab, Dimitri's, Fresco's, Mykonos, Mahuffer's, Undertow, El Cap, Brighter Days, Shephard's Tiki Bar, Casa Tina). Also: Visit Sarasota for Lucky 8, FOX 13 for the Seahorse and Rod & Reel, and I Love the Burg for Frenchy's Saltwater Cafe.

## How candidates were found

1. Visit St. Pete-Clearwater lists, read with WebFetch: the Eat & Drink dining hub, "Landmark Restaurants", "Best Waterfront Restaurants", "MICHELIN-Recognized Restaurants", the Gulp Coast Craft Beer Trail (north, central and south region pages), Drinks, Nightlife, "Best Rooftop Bars & Restaurants" and the LGBTQ travel page. The individual profiles were used for addresses, phones and hours where a business site blocked us.
2. The MICHELIN Guide 2026 Florida announcement on michelinmedia.com (read with curl; the full Bib Gourmand, starred and recommended tables are images on that page and were read one by one). guide.michelin.com returned empty pages to both fetchers.
3. Visit Sarasota's Michelin article, WWSB/mysuncoast (Tralia and the first Sarasota Michelin picks) and the Columbia Restaurant locations page.
4. The St. Pete Pier restaurants page (stpetepier.org/restaurants) and the SpongeDocks.net Tarpon Springs restaurant list.
5. News checks for storm damage and closures: FOX 13 (Seahorse reopening, Rod & Reel moving on land, Central Park food hall), I Love the Burg (Frenchy's reopenings, Nov 2024) and Axios (Cycle Brewing taproom closing).
6. Search: the session's WebSearch budget was already used up, and Bing/DuckDuckGo/Google HTML pages were blocked or broken, so discovery used Marginalia Search (via curl) plus direct fetches of known official sites.
7. Quotes: every quote was checked against page text read with curl, or taken from a page read directly. Quotes that reached me only through WebFetch's summarizer (mostly Visit St. Pete-Clearwater profiles, and Visit Sarasota for Lucky 8) were dropped, because two reads of the same page returned different wording. 68 records have a quote.

## Deliberately left out (and why)

- **Cycle Brewing** (St. Pete): Axios (May 6, 2025) reported the downtown taproom closing. The article itself was blocked, and cyclebrewing.com shows "This store is unavailable". Current status is not confirmed.
- **Frenchy's Original Cafe and Frenchy's South Beach Cafe**: frenchysonline.com blocks both fetchers, and no readable page gives their current addresses. I Love the Burg (Nov 2024) says the original cafe had reopened.
- **Woody's Waterfront** (St. Pete Beach): the site's domain did not resolve, and there was no tourism profile.
- **Coney Island Grill** (St. Pete, hot dogs): coneyislandgrill.com is now an unrelated template site, and the status could not be confirmed. **Munch's** had no site found.
- **Flanagan's Irish Pub** (Dunedin): its domain is for sale, and the status is unconfirmed.
- **Merry Pier** (Pass-a-Grille bait shop and pier) is left to the outdoors/see slices, and its status is unknown. The **Anna Maria City Pier** restaurant and **Beach House** (Bradenton Beach) are not covered.
- **Chains and hotel lobby bars** without a local story; **Kahwa Coffee** (a St. Pete-founded chain with no single flagship identified); Crabby Bill's St. Pete Beach and Palm Harbor branches (mentioned in the main record); smaller Gulp Coast breweries (Bayboro, Overflow, Grand Central Brewhouse, Cueni, HOB, Woodwright, Soggy Bottom, Stilt House, de Bine, Two Frogs, Unrefined, Arkane, Southern Lights, Sea Dog, Mastry's Brewing, Troubled Waters).
- **Palm Harbor and Oldsmar** have no records; nothing there met the brief's "historic or signature" bar in the lists read.
- **Sarasota** is limited to Michelin picks, the Columbia and Yoder's (historic), as the brief asked.

## Open questions for the verifier

1. **Seahorse Restaurant (Pass-a-Grille)**: FOX 13 (Jan 26, 2026) said it would reopen the next week. Confirm it is serving and add its street address. The record has no address or coordinates.
2. **Rod & Reel Pier**: the pier was washed away by Milton. Is the Holmes Beach replacement (former Old Hamburg Schnitzelhaus) open, and at what address? Is the pier being rebuilt?
3. **Status from tourism profiles only** (no official site readable): Frenchy's Rockaway Grill (reported still recovering in Nov 2024; profile now lists hours), Mykonos (Facebook page only), Mahuffer's, Undertow, Billy's Stone Crab, Dimitri's, El Cap.
4. **Hours left unknown because sources disagree**: in between days, Tralia, Tarpon Springs Distillery, Mama's Greek Cuisine, Star Fish Company.
5. **Area judgment calls**: Ted Peters is in the city of South Pasadena (filed under west-stpete); Harvey's and El Cap (4th St N at 31st–35th Ave) are filed under old-northeast.
6. **Own claims, quoted and attributed only**: Dunedin Brewery ("oldest distributing microbrewery still in operation"), Green Bench ("St. Petersburg's first microbrewery"), Crabby's Beachside Pavilion ("oldest beach pavilion in Florida"), Columbia St. Armands ("oldest operating restaurant in Sarasota"), Caretta on the Gulf ("Clearwater's only AAA Four-Diamond" restaurant), Parkshore Grill ("first major restaurant" on Beach Drive), Anecdote ("closest brewery to the Gulf beach").
